title: 的 / 地 / 得 Step 1 · Before a Noun, Before a Verb: 的 and 地
description: Three characters, one sound. Start with two: 的 links a describer to a **noun**, 地 links a describer to a **verb**.

points.title: 的 + noun: whose? which? what kind?
points.summary: 的 hangs a describer onto a noun: 我的书, 漂亮的衣服, 我昨天买的书.
points.body:
- **我的**书 my book
- **漂亮的**衣服 pretty clothes
- **我昨天买的**书 the book I bought yesterday — a whole clause can describe the noun.

Whatever comes after 的 is a **thing** (noun).

| | comes before … | pattern | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **的** | a **noun** | describer + 的 + noun | 漂亮**的**衣服 · 我买**的**书 |
| **地** | a **verb** (how it's done) | describer + 地 + verb | 慢慢**地**走 · 认真**地**学习 |
| **得** | the **result** (after the verb) | verb / adj. + 得 + how | 跑**得**很快 · 累**得**不想动 |

**The trick:** look **right** — a noun next → 的, a verb next → 地. Look **left** — a verb or adjective just before → 得. (All three are read *de*.)
examples: This is the book I bought yesterday.

points.title: 地 + verb: how is it done?
points.summary: 地 hangs a describer onto a verb: 慢慢地走 (walk slowly), 认真地学习 (study hard).
points.body:
- 他**慢慢地**走进了教室。 He slowly walked into the classroom.
- 她**高兴地**说：「我考上了！」 She said happily …

Whatever comes after 地 is an **action** (verb). In casual writing people often type 的 here — tests want 地.

| | comes before … | pattern | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| **的** | a **noun** | describer + 的 + noun | 漂亮**的**衣服 · 我买**的**书 |
| **地** | a **verb** (how it's done) | describer + 地 + verb | 慢慢**地**走 · 认真**地**学习 |
| **得** | the **result** (after the verb) | verb / adj. + 得 + how | 跑**得**很快 · 累**得**不想动 |

**The trick:** look **right** — a noun next → 的, a verb next → 地. Look **left** — a verb or adjective just before → 得. (All three are read *de*.)

questions.prompt: 的 or 地? Look at the word right **after** the blank.
notes: 菜 is a noun → 的.
说 is a verb → 地.
衣服 is a noun → 的.
书 is a noun → 的.
学习 (to study) is a verb here → 地.
走 is a verb → 地.

questions.prompt: Build it: 'This is the book I bought yesterday.'
questions.explanation: 这是**我昨天买的书**。 The whole 'I bought yesterday' describes 书, glued on with 的.
questions.translation: This is the book I bought yesterday.

questions.prompt: Build it: 'He slowly walked into the classroom.'
questions.explanation: 他**慢慢地走进**了教室。 How he walked (慢慢) + 地 + the verb.
questions.translation: He slowly walked into the classroom.

questions.prompt: What always comes right after 地?
questions.explanation: 地 + **verb**: 慢慢地走, 认真地学习.
notes: 地 never ends a sentence: something must be done 'slowly', 'happily' …
No — 地 links to how something is done.
That's 的: 漂亮的衣服.

questions.prompt: Which phrases are correct (standard written Chinese)? Select all.
notes: 写 is a verb → 地. ✔
走 is a verb → 慢慢**地**走 (的 here is casual, not standard).
手机 is a noun → 的. ✔
Whose? → 我**的**书.
衣服 is a noun → 漂亮**的**衣服.
笑 is a verb → 地. ✔

questions.prompt: In 「{我|wǒ}{昨天|zuótiān}{买|mǎi}{的|de}{书|shū}」, what is 的 doing?
options: Nothing — it could be left out
notes: 的 isn't a tense marker — 昨天 shows the time.
Not quite: the describer comes **before** the noun, the reverse of 'of'.
Without 的 it isn't a phrase any more.

questions.prompt: 的 phrases: match each to its meaning.
questions.explanation: Everything before 的 describes the noun after it.
notes: 我 + 的 = whose.
很贵 describes 手机.
昨天来 describes 人.
我买 + 的 = which book: the one I bought.

questions.prompt: Round 2 — 的 or 地? (Careful: the same word can go either way.)
questions.explanation: Same describer (努力, 开心), different job: it depends on what comes **next**.
notes: 关上 is a verb → 地.
玩 is a verb → 地.
工作 (to work) is the action → 努力地工作.
首都 is a noun → 的.
学生 is a noun → 努力的学生.
周末 is a noun → 的.
